pr_title: Wait longer for pod cleanup in tests
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
When TestPreemptWithPermitPlugin failed, we can see the following in test output:

```
I0810 18:10:36.998037  110601 factory.go:622] Attempting to bind signalling-pod to test-node-1
...
E0810 18:11:28.006187  110601 factory.go:606] Error getting pod permit-plugin084312fc-62d2-435e-9676-9c160c9a83c4/signalling-pod for retry: Get http://127.0.0.1:44639/api/v1/namespaces/permit-plugin084312fc-62d2-435e-9676-9c160c9a83c4/pods/signalling-pod: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:44639: connect: connection refused; retrying...
```
It seems the signallingPod from other subtest was not cleaned up properly.

This PR makes the waiting period longer for cleanup.
Also adds assertion that signallingPod is cleaned up in the related test.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #81238

```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

```docs

```

Thanks for it! I am looking into it too.

> I0810 18:10:36.998037  110601 factory.go:622] Attempting to bind signalling-pod to test-node-1

For this log, I am not sure why it tries to attempt bind a pod before scheduling it when a scheduler starts.

comments:
Another flaky https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/81006#pullrequestreview-271138457

https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/81006/pull-kubernetes-integration/1158614573872320512/ 

```go
--- FAIL: TestPreemptWithPermitPlugin (64.95s)
    framework_test.go:1618: Expected the preemptor pod to be scheduled. error: timed out waiting for the condition
    framework_test.go:1622: Expected the waiting pod to get preempted and deleted
```

It happens at 2019-08-06 05:43:47 +0000 UTC

```
I0810 03:03:26.425702  110762 factory.go:557] Unable to schedule preempt-with-permit-plugin8c137daf-8329-4b96-9319-9fbe8fa8ae1f/preemptor-pod: no fit: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu, 1 Insufficient memory.; waiting
```
The above repeated for 30 seconds.

I checked the code and log again. I think the reason is as following:

When scheduler preempted `waiting-pod`, it failed to delete the pod(same as the case for `signaling-pod`, there might be something wrong with etcd), so it could not schedule `preemptor-pod` because `waiting-pod` had not been deleted successfully.

/assign

Find the root cause now, will send a PR soon.
@tedyu Thanks for your work! Not sure whether you are still investigating it, the flaky test is impacting many PRs now, so I send a PR for it now, sorry for it.

review_comments: Why are we updating the timeout, it does not sound correct.

See the log snippet from description.
This gives signallingPod clean up more time.
If unfinished cleanup caused the flaky, update this would only decrease the odds of flaky.
Do you have suggestion how clean up can be made more robust ?

tests that use this package variable should be expected to complete in O(ms) or O(single-digit seconds). Nothing that gets anywhere close to 30 seconds in normal execution should make use of this.

There are two possibilities for this flake:
* normal execution sometimes takes longer than 30 seconds, but then completes. if that is the case, we need to demonstrate the path(s) that cause this, and either optimize them (preferred), or specifically lengthen the timeout for those test paths (not change the global "Forever" timeout)
* a bug in the test sometimes makes pod deletion hang. If that is the case, lengthening this will not help.

Agree with both points above.

I can spend more time on #2, after wrapping up some of my other PRs.
